transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, what made me come in is that... the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat. And heavy, I guess. 

Like, I usually do these photography walks, and I mentor some kids, or even just keeping a clean calendar at work—I'm an executive secretary, so I'm usually really on top of that stuff. But lately, I just stopped initiating them. It's like I just don't have the drive to start any of it right now.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

I haven't really had a period quite like this before, no. This specific feeling... it's been going on for about a year and three months now. 

It started right after a family member of mine had some sudden changes in their health and behavior, and I had to step in and take on a lot more coordination for them. I just haven't really bounced back to my normal self since then.

During this past year and three months, have there been any stretches of two weeks or longer where your mood felt significantly lower, or where you lost interest in almost everything, even more intensely than you feel right now?

No, not really. It's just been this... steady sort of flat feeling the whole time. It hasn't dipped into anything deeper or more intense for a couple of weeks like you're asking. Just this constant lack of drive since all that stuff happened with my family.
During this year and three months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as sleeping much more or much less than you normally do?

Yeah, actually, I have. Um, I've been sleeping a lot less on certain nights. 

There have been times when I only get maybe two or three hours of sleep, and I'll wake up way before dawn. But the thing is, I don't feel tired at all. I just feel completely ready to go—like I'm ready to start answering work emails or updating appointment lists instead of just trying to go back to sleep.
During those nights when you sleep very little and feel ready to go, do you find yourself feeling unusually talkative, having racing thoughts, or feeling more confident than usual?

Yeah, I definitely get a lot more talkative. My wife and some of my coworkers have actually pointed it out to me. They tell me I talk so fast during those periods that I'll just jump straight from going over medical forms, right into my work deadlines, and then onto some new mentoring ideas I have. 

I guess I just keep going and going before they can even get a word in edgewise. So, yes, that definitely happens.
When you have these periods where you feel energetic, talkative, and don't need much sleep, how many days in a row do those specific episodes usually last?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of exactly how many days in a row it happens. It just kind of comes on, and I'm going a hundred miles an hour, but I couldn't give you a specific number of days.

During those periods where you feel energetic and talkative, does your behavior ever become so intense that it causes major problems at work or in your relationships, or have you ever had to be hospitalized because of it?

No, nothing like that. I mean, my wife gets a little annoyed when I'm talking a mile a minute, and maybe my coworkers think I'm being a bit much, but it hasn't caused any major problems. I've never been in trouble at work over it, and I've definitely never had to go to the hospital or anything. It's just... I just have a lot of energy, you know? But I still get my work done.

During those times when you are sleeping very little and talking fast, do you feel that your mood is clearly different, such as feeling unusually happy, euphoric, or irritable, compared to how you usually feel?

Yeah, it definitely is. I have these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, like I'm just sure everything is clicking perfectly. But then... well, a tiny change, like someone moving a meeting on the calendar, can make me really sharp with people. It happens in a way that actually surprises me, to be honest.
